page: The Microsoft Azure E4bs_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine deployed under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is driven by an x86_64 Intel processor featuring 4 dedicated virtual CPUs. System memory totals 32.0 GB, delivering an 8.0 GB per-core allocation ratio. This high memory-to-vCPU ratio supports memory-intensive applications that require extensive working sets without necessitating excessive core counts.

Architecturally, the E4bs_v6 does not include onboard local storage disks or hardware accelerator components such as GPUs. All disk storage operations rely entirely on remote block storage interfaces, with the Ebsv6 series specifically architected for enhanced block storage performance and Premium Storage compatibility. The absence of local solid-state storage eliminates ephemeral drive overhead, directing infrastructure cost toward dedicated compute allocation, large memory buffers, and sustained remote storage throughput.

By isolating persistent data onto remote block volumes while dedicating 32.0 GB of RAM across 4 cores, the E4bs_v6 provides balanced resource efficiency for memory-heavy environments. The instance is suitable for hosting relational database management systems, transactional caching platforms, enterprise resource management workloads, and data ingestion services where RAM density and reliable storage subsystems take precedence over raw compute scaling.
description: The Microsoft Azure E4bs_v6 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Powered by an Intel processor, the instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs alongside 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB memory-to-core allocation ratio. Hardware acceleration features such as discrete GPUs are not present, and the instance includes no local ephemeral storage. Instead, the Ebsv6 series is architecturally tailored for high-performance remote block storage, including Azure Premium Storage compatibility, shifting persistent disk operations entirely to network-attached block volumes. Because the virtual machine does not package integrated NVMe or local scratch drives, resource utilization focuses on memory density and external storage I/O bandwidth. This architectural tradeoff delivers cost efficiency for environments requiring strong RAM capacity and consistent managed storage rather than high-density local disks. The E4bs_v6 is appropriate for relational database engines, in-memory caches, enterprise applications, and transactional workloads.
